Booking amount means bookings.final_amount, the amount actually paid after discounts. Use bookings.final_amount for any average, sum, minimum, maximum or comparison of a booking amount or booking value. Do not use bookings.actual_amount (the price before discount) unless the question explicitly says 'actual amount' or 'original amount'.
A completed booking is a row in bookings with bookings.status = 1. Apply this filter only when the question explicitly asks for completed or successful bookings.

Discount value is the mathematical difference between offer.actual_price and offer.offer_price. Always calculate it as (actual_price - offer_price). Do not look for a 'discount' column in the offer table.

Savings uses the code-owned numeric metric named savings for selection, filtering, ranking, and AVG/SUM when requested. Include valid positive price reductions, including an offer price of 1; exclude zero or negative final prices and non-positive savings. Do not substitute a single price column or ask the model to write an expression.

Offer discount percentage uses the code-owned discount_percent metric. When actual_price and a positive offer_price form a valid reduction, calculate (actual_price - offer_price) * 100 / actual_price. If offer_price is NULL, use offer_price_p only when it is between 1 and 100. If both price and percentage values exist, the derived and stored percentages must agree within one percentage point; otherwise the value is ambiguous and excluded. Zero-price giveaways are not discounts. Use coupon_discount_percent only for coupon-level percentage questions; it reads coupon_price_p and is never combined with the offer-level percentage. Keep percentage thresholds separate from currency metrics.
Coupon-level percentage discount is the code-owned coupon_discount_percent metric, sourced from coupon_price_p when it is between 1 and 100. Do not combine it with the offer-level discount_percent.

Exact state-name comparisons ignore letter case, leading/trailing whitespace, and ordinary spaces within a state name. This supports formatting variants such as 'Tamil Nadu' and 'tamilnadu'; it does not correct misspellings or replace canonical state values at data ingestion.

For a percentage, use the code-owned share_of_rows metric with ONE simple numeric comparison describing only what counts in the numerator (for example, rating = 5). Any scope limiting the denominator rows, such as a date range, status, or shop, belongs in where_expression. Example: 'percentage of reviews created in 2025 rated five stars' uses condition reviews.rating = 5 and where_expression created_at >= '2025-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-01-01'. For an unscoped percentage (the case #39 shape), 'percentage of reviews rated five stars' uses condition reviews.rating = 5 and no where_expression. The denominator is every base-table row after where_expression is applied, including rows with NULL condition values. This metric does not define ratios between two independently counted groups or conditions on text columns.
General wording about posted offers includes every offer status. Filter offer.status = 1 only when the user explicitly asks for active or currently active offers.

An active offer means offer.status = 1. For generic active-offer questions, do not add a date condition or a shop_details.status filter; when the question explicitly requests a time window, apply the corresponding temporal business rule in addition to offer.status = 1. When counting reviews for shops that have active offers, use verified joins and COUNT(DISTINCT reviews.id) so multiple matching offers do not duplicate reviews. For any question about active offers, use the offer table (offer.status = 1) as the table that holds the offers and join it to shop_details through the verified offer-to-shop relationship. Do not use editable_offers_view for active-offer questions, because it has no verified relationship to the other tables.

For store, regional, or booking metrics grouped or filtered by city, the approved booking/store city is shop_address.city on the booked shop's default address (shop_address.is_default = 1), reached through the verified shop_id relationship. bookings.city is unvalidated free text and may contain spelling errors and casing variants; it must not be used in WHERE filters or GROUP BY. If a request explicitly asks to display the city typed on a booking record, it may be selected as raw descriptive text only, without filtering or grouping on it. Do not compensate with query-level LOWER or TRIM wrappers. For a distinct count or list of shops by city, area, or location, use the default address and count shop IDs distinctly. When asked to show a shop's address or landmark details, select shop_address.arearoadname, shop_address.nearbylandmark, shop_address.city, and shop_address.pincode, using the default address as representative. The exact landmark column is nearbylandmark. Use any matching address only when the user explicitly asks for all addresses, any address, or a delivery address; otherwise default-address filtering prevents duplicate shop or offer rows.

A 'products' table exists but must not be used, because some offers reference products that no longer exist. To list what a shop offers, select offer_heading and product_name from offer_items_view for that shop. product_name can be empty. Label offer_heading as 'Offer heading' and product_name as 'Product name'. To find which shops offer a given item, use the pipeline's text search operation.

When a question asks for the volume, number, or traffic of reservations or bookings, it strictly requires a count of distinct records. Always calculate this using COUNT(DISTINCT bookings.id) to prevent multi-table join fan-out. Do NOT use SUM(bookings.final_amount) unless the prompt explicitly asks for revenue, sales, earnings, or monetary value.

The offer table connects to categories through shop_details. To filter, aggregate, or list offers by category, join offer to shop_details via reviewed_offer_shop_id, and then shop_details to categories via reviewed_shop_details_category_id.
An active user is a row in users with users.status = 1. Apply that status filter when the question explicitly asks for active users.
An active shop is a row in shop_details with shop_details.status = 1. Use this status only when the request asks for active shops or a current-state active shop condition.
An inactive shop is a row in shop_details with shop_details.status = 0. Use this status only when the request asks for inactive shops or a current-state inactive shop condition.

synonyms: plan is the most popular among our users
terms.definition: Users are linked to plans by users.plan_id = plans.id. A user having an assigned plan means users.plan_id IS NOT NULL. Enforce plans.status = 1 for pricing and subscription-plan queries. When asked which plan is most popular among users, count active users (users.status = 1) per active plan, group by the plan, and order by that count descending.

For every pricing or subscription-plan query, include only plans with plans.status = 1. Join users.plan_id to plans.id when relating subscribers to plans. Filter users.status = 1 only when counting active subscriber accounts or when the question explicitly asks for active users; an assigned plan is identified by users.plan_id IS NOT NULL.

synonyms: monthly recurring revenue from active subscribers
terms.definition: Potential recurring revenue (MRR) must be rooted at users, not calculated directly on the plans table alone. Join users.plan_id = plans.id, require users.status = 1, users.subscriber_status = 1, users.plan_id IS NOT NULL, and plans.status = 1, then calculate SUM(plans.price) once per qualifying active subscriber account. Never calculate recurring revenue directly on the plans table alone.

For booking-volume or booking-revenue questions scoped by when bookings were received or revenue was generated, use bookings.created_at. Use bookings.time_slot_date only when the user explicitly asks for the appointment, scheduled slot, or service date.

Offer-view activity is recorded in the views table. Join views.offer_id to offer.id, count views.id per offer, and use offer.status = 1 when ranking offers for discovery. Do not substitute callviews for views.

Rank shops by the average of non-NULL reviews.rating values. Shops without reviews are excluded. Do not impose a minimum review count unless the user asks for one. Return only the number of rows requested by the user; a 'which shop' request is singular.

For this database, good or highly rated restaurants are active shops (shop_details.status = 1) in subcategories.subcategoryname = 'Restaurent' whose average reviews.rating is at least 4. Join shop_details to subcategories, shop_address, and reviews using verified relationships; filter shop_address.is_default = 1 and apply any requested city filter to that default address.

A service is free when its price is zero or an explicit free flag or tag marks it as free. When the service is represented by an offer, use offer.offer_price = 0; use a free flag or tag only when that field exists in the retrieved schema. Count distinct shop IDs when counting shops. Apply an active-offer status filter only when the question requests currently available or active offers.

Treat a user as unverified when users.status = 0 or users.is_verified = 0, using only the corresponding verification/status fields present in the retrieved schema and never inventing a column. A purchase is a transaction whose payment status is 1. When coupon_purchase_payment is present, join it to users through coupon_purchase_payment.user_id = users.id and require coupon_purchase_payment.status = 1.

synonyms: users signed up in the last 7 days ending on the most recent signup date
7 days ending on the most recent signup date
signups in the latest seven-day period
users who signed up in the last seven days
terms.definition: Anchor the signup window to the latest recorded signup date in users.created_at, not the request clock. Include the latest signup date and the six preceding calendar dates by filtering users.created_at >= (SELECT MAX(DATE(created_at)) FROM users) - INTERVAL 6 DAY. Return an anonymous count when the user asks how many users signed up; do not project email or other personal contact details.

synonyms: plans allowing more than a number of products
plans with a product limit above
plans that allow more products than
terms.definition: Compare the requested product threshold against plans.product_limit. Include only active plans with plans.status = 1.

synonyms: active users do not have a plan assigned
active users who do not have a plan assigned
terms.definition: A user without an assigned plan has users.plan_id IS NULL or users.plan_id = 0. When the request asks for active users without a plan, require users.status = 1 and combine the missing-plan alternatives with OR inside parentheses.
A partner account is a row in users with users.user_type = 2. Do not count customers with user_type = 1; apply other status filters only when the question asks for them.

For the insurance-document audit, select active shops with shop_details.status = 1 whose shop_details.insurance is NULL or the empty string. Treat the missing-document predicate as (shop_details.insurance IS NULL OR shop_details.insurance = ''). Do not include shops with a non-empty insurance path.

For insurance and compliance-document audits, query shop_details and include only active shops where shop_details.status = 1 and the document path is missing: shop_details.insurance IS NULL OR shop_details.insurance = ''. The schema has no insurance expiration-date column, so 'expired' or 'invalid' wording means a missing document path only; do not claim to verify an expiration date.

Measure service-offer popularity by counting views.id through views.offer_id = offer.id, then associate the offer with service through offer.service_id = service.id. Include only active offers (offer.status = 1) that represent a service (offer.service_id > 0). offer.offer_type is numeric in the schema and has no verified string enum mapping; do not compare it to the string 'service'. Group by service and rank by the view count.

synonyms: shops with both product and service offers
shops that offer products and services
shops with product and service offers
both an active product offer and an active service offer
terms.definition: Count shops with at least one active product offer and at least one active service offer. On offer rows require status = 1, and detect product/service capability with product_id > 0 and service_id > 0 respectively (zero is the stored no-assignment value). Group by shop_id and require SUM(CASE WHEN product_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 and SUM(CASE WHEN service_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0; count the qualifying shops, not offer rows.

synonyms: both an active product offer and an active service offer
shops with product and service offers
terms.definition: Shops offering both products and services simultaneously must have at least one active product offer AND at least one active service offer. Product and service assignments are indicated by product_id > 0 and service_id > 0; require status = 1, group by shop_id, and count qualifying shops rather than offer rows. Canonical SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT shop_id FROM offer WHERE status = 1 GROUP BY shop_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN product_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN service_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0) t.
terms.canonical_sql_pattern: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT shop_id FROM offer WHERE status = 1 GROUP BY shop_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN product_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN service_id > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0) t

terms.definition: For active offers ending in the current calendar month, require offer.status = 1 and filter offer.end_date using the half-open bounded range end_date >= CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL (DAYOFMONTH(CURRENT_DATE()) - 1) DAY AND end_date < (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL (DAYOFMONTH(CURRENT_DATE()) - 1) DAY) + INTERVAL 1 MONTH. Use the typed current_month_start and next_month_start calendar-boundary values; do not use DATE_FORMAT, table MIN/MAX dates, or fixed literal parameters.
terms.canonical_sql_pattern: SELECT offer_heading, end_date FROM offer WHERE status = 1 AND end_date >= CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL (DAYOFMONTH(CURRENT_DATE()) - 1) DAY AND end_date < (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL (DAYOFMONTH(CURRENT_DATE()) - 1) DAY) + INTERVAL 1 MONTH

synonyms: views between 2 and 4 in the morning
terms.definition: For time-of-day view filters use the validated HOUR function on views.created_at, a TIMESTAMP column. The 2 AM through 4 AM example is HOUR(created_at) BETWEEN 2 AND 4. Numeric hour bounds must be integers from 0 to 23.

synonyms: which shops have uploaded all 3 product images for their offers
shops that uploaded all 3 product images
shops with all three product images
offers with all product image slots populated
all product images uploaded for offers
terms.definition: This is a universal condition: a qualifying shop must have at least one offer, and EVERY offer for that shop must have product_img1, product_img2, and product_img3 all IS NOT NULL. Anchor on shop_details, require an EXISTS offer for the shop, and exclude the shop if its id appears in the set of non-NULL offer.shop_id values with any image slot IS NULL. This anti-join avoids treating one complete offer as proof that all offers are complete; do not use an existential image filter or HAVING aggregates over images.
terms.canonical_sql_pattern: SELECT DISTINCT sd.id, sd.name FROM shop_details sd WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o WHERE o.shop_id = sd.id) AND sd.id NOT IN (SELECT o.shop_id FROM offer o WHERE o.shop_id IS NOT NULL AND (o.product_img1 IS NULL OR o.product_img2 IS NULL OR o.product_img3 IS NULL))

synonyms: uploaded all 3 product images for their offers
terms.definition: To find shops where EVERY offer has all 3 images, require at least one offer and exclude any shop that has at least one offer missing an image. Use the NOT IN anti-join with shop_id IS NOT NULL to avoid NULL poisoning: offer.product_img1 IS NULL OR offer.product_img2 IS NULL OR offer.product_img3 IS NULL. This is universal quantification across all offers, not a search for shops with one complete offer.
terms.canonical_sql_pattern: SELECT DISTINCT sd.id, sd.name FROM shop_details sd WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer o WHERE o.shop_id = sd.id) AND sd.id NOT IN (SELECT o.shop_id FROM offer o WHERE o.shop_id IS NOT NULL AND (o.product_img1 IS NULL OR o.product_img2 IS NULL OR o.product_img3 IS NULL))

synonyms: shop categories get viewed the most
terms.definition: Count views.id by shop category through the verified contiguous path views.offer_id -> offer.id -> offer.shop_id -> shop_details.id -> shop_details.category_id -> categories.id. Group by category identity/name and order by the view count descending.

Interpret the last six months as a rolling six-calendar-month window anchored to the current test or request clock in the configured business timezone. Resolve it once to explicit ISO 8601 start and exclusive end dates, then bind those dates as parameters in generated SQL. Tests should freeze the resolver clock to their test anchor and evaluate the oracle against that same anchor.
Tracking page visits or users checking out a shop profile corresponds to counting records in the views table grouped by shop_id (COUNT(views.id)).
A 'really bad' or 'worst' rating represents the minimum rating floor: reviews.rating = 1 for the lowest rating, or MIN(reviews.rating) when the question asks for the observed minimum.
Ride and personal transport requests map to subcategories with subcategories.subcategoryname IN ('Taxi', 'Auto Rickshaw').

synonyms: compare views and bookings across categories
terms.definition: Compare category-level view and booking counts using independent grouped subqueries, never by joining views and bookings together in the same aggregate input. Aggregate views and bookings separately through their verified many-to-one paths to shop_details and categories, then join each result by category id. Represent each metric as a separate isolated_child_aggregates operation with its verified relationship_path; do not use a cross-joined child metric plan.
terms.canonical_sql_pattern: SELECT c.categoriesname, COALESCE(v.total_views, 0) AS total_views, COALESCE(b.total_bookings, 0) AS total_bookings, COALESCE(v.total_views, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(b.total_bookings, 0), 0) AS view_booking_ratio FROM categories c LEFT JOIN (SELECT sd.category_id, COUNT(v.id) AS total_views FROM views v JOIN shop_details sd ON v.shop_id = sd.id GROUP BY sd.category_id) v ON v.category_id = c.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT sd.category_id, COUNT(b.id) AS total_bookings FROM bookings b JOIN shop_details sd ON b.shop_id = sd.id GROUP BY sd.category_id) b ON b.category_id = c.id
